t: Peter I reigned from 1682 to 1725, sole ruler from 1696, and in 1721 took the title Emperor of All Russia after victory over Sweden in the Great Northern War.

He founded Saint Petersburg in 1703 and made it the capital, built a navy, and reorganised the state through the Governing Senate, the collegia, the Table of Ranks and a Holy Synod that replaced the patriarchate.

His reforms were imposed by force: he crushed revolts such as the Streltsy and Bulavin rebellions, and historians still argue whether he set Russia on a modern course or, as Evgeny Anisimov put it, created an administrative command system.
dyk: Boyars who wished to keep their beards after Peter's return from Western Europe had to pay an annual beard tax of one hundred rubles.
ev: Peter and his half-brother Ivan V are proclaimed joint tsars, with their sister Sophia as regent
Peter overthrows Sophia's regency and sends her to a convent
Peter's new fleet helps capture the Ottoman fortress of Azov
Peter sets out on the Grand Embassy to Western Europe
Peter founds Saint Petersburg on Hare Island
The Russians decisively defeat Charles XII of Sweden at the Battle of Poltava
The Treaty of Nystad ends the Great Northern War and Peter is proclaimed Emperor of All Russia
Peter dies of a bladder illness and is buried in the Saints Peter and Paul Cathedral

f.born: 9 June 1672; son of Tsar Alexei Mikailovich and his second wife Natalya Naryshkina, of the Romanov dynasty
f.died: 8 February 1725, between four and five in the morning, of an illness of the bladder found at autopsy to be gangrenous; buried in the Saints Peter and Paul Cathedral
f.role: Tsar of all Russia, 1682–1721 (jointly with Ivan V until 1696); Emperor of All Russia, 1721–1725
f.known: The Great Northern War and the victory at Poltava; founding Saint Petersburg; the Russian Navy; the Grand Embassy to Western Europe; the Governing Senate, the collegia and the Table of Ranks; the Holy Synod in place of the patriarchate
